findings.title: D-031 copy-back regression: finish() raises an unhandled FileExistsError (exit 1, no sandbox.json, possible partial copy-back) when the same own-role path appears in the real directory during the run, where the round-16 code discarded it cleanly (fail-closed; observation)
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py:259 tests `rel in seed` (the staging seed) instead of the live real directory, and line 266 then opens the destination with O_EXCL. If the real file was created after prepare (for example by a second concurrent run of the same role), the file is not in the seed, so the write-once discard branch is skipped and os.open raises FileExistsError. The loop is not wrapped, so the files sorted after it are not copied and sandbox.json is not written. Reproduced in a disposable fixture (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-17/r17-copyback-ipc-repro.mjs, case D; log 04-copyback-ipc-repro.log): round-16 code: exit 3 with the entry discarded as 'existing file changed; review files are write-once'; round-17 code: exit 1 with a FileExistsError traceback and no sandbox.json. The real file is not overwritten.
findings.expected: A collision with an existing real file is reported as a discard (exit 3), sandbox.json is always written, and no partial copy-back occurs. For example, check os.path.lexists(dest) for the non-replace case, or catch FileExistsError and record a discard.
findings.actual: Unhandled exception. This fails closed: run-agent.sh:236-240 treats any non-zero finish status as exit 73 (not auto-committed) for confined roles, and the validator requires sandbox.json (rules.mjs:352-354), so gate integrity is not affected. But the runner's message wrongly says writes were 'discarded', evidence is missing, and earlier-sorted files may already have been copied back. It needs concurrent runs of the same role, which the protocol does not schedule. I would accept this as an observation.

findings.title: agent_sandbox.py module docstring misstates the confinement: it says 'the PID and IPC namespaces are private', but the PID namespace is shared with the host (threat-model residual 8)
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py:23-25 (module docstring) states 'no_new_privs is set, the PID and IPC namespaces are private'. bwrap_args (line 145) passes only --unshare-ipc, with no --unshare-pid, and the code comment at lines 134-144, threat-model.md residual 8 and sandbox.json (unshare: ["ipc"]) all correctly say that the PID namespace is shared.
findings.expected: The docstring matches the implementation and the threat model: private IPC namespace; shared host PID namespace (disclosed residual 8).
findings.actual: The docstring overstates the isolation. This is documentation only: the machine-readable evidence (sandbox.json) and the threat model are correct. I would accept this as an observation.
